concerns.text: FR-010 mandates calculating SD for entropy tolerance 'r' using ONLY time points remaining after motion scrubbing. Task T015b and T046 explicitly instruct to compute SD on the 'N=120 truncated series' (implying truncation happens before SD calculation). This creates a coverage gap where the task implementation contradicts the spec's data hygiene requirement, leaving FR-010 un-satisfiable by the current task definition.

FR-008 requires the baseline connectivity model to use PCA reduced to exactly 200 components. While T023a covers this, Task T023c introduces a 'Feature Selection' step reducing features to a 'smaller subset' and T024b trains on this reduced set. The tasks lack a clear, unambiguous instruction that the PRIMARY baseline comparison for SC-001/SC-002 must strictly use the 200-component set (T023a) and not the reduced set, risking implementation of the wrong baseline.

SC-003 requires 1,000 permutation iterations for statistical validity. Task T051 introduces a 'dry-run' mode with 10 iterations, and T042 caps a performance test at 50 subjects/6 hours. There is no explicit task instruction to execute the full 1,000 iterations on the CI runner or a verification step ensuring the full count is run, creating a gap in satisfying the success criterion.

FR-009 requires imputing zero-variance parcels with the 'median entropy value of that specific parcel across the entire cohort'. Task T015c performs this imputation during the subject loop but lacks a preceding task to calculate and store the cohort-wide medians before the loop begins. Without this, the task cannot technically fulfill the 'acentire cohort' requirement without an implicit, unspecified full-pass operation.

FR-007 requires exclusions to be logged to 'exclusions.log'. Task T005b logs to 'data/raw/exclusions.log', but Task T039 generates a 'motion_confound_report.json'. The tasks do not explicitly link the exclusion log to the final report generation, creating ambiguity about whether the exclusion logging requirement is fully satisfied in the final deliverable.
